scope: Reviewed the saved review scope, v1 protocol, config, entry contract, prior-art note, stage gate, EXP-0024 protocol/result and original model/refresh source. No training, prototype fitting, evaluation input or research run was executed.
checks: The 12 seeds 25001..25012 produce 24 newly trained REL/INV models at 1000 updates each; the two frozen 23005 checkpoints are reference models only. Twenty-six calibration fits yield 52 prototypes. The 24,000 research updates, 104 qualification cells, 520 final cells, 624 total cells, 42,172,416 final-plus-qualification transition tokens, 106,496 calibration tokens and 8,256,000 training transition tokens agree with the registered dimensions. Runtime feasibility is not established by arithmetic.

The qualification and final roots differ. REL IID/prototype qualification and LONG failure/success strata are determined on qualification data using NONE; the final test then measures repair. A qualification failure that does not recur on final NONE remains in the original failure denominator and cannot count as repaired. The old 23005 reference is outside both new-seed R and M denominators. No extra failed seeds may be recruited.

The affine Gram readout implies z(sqrt(alpha) P) = b + alpha (z_P-b) and z(sqrt(beta) H) = b + beta (z-b) in exact arithmetic. Thus alpha=(z-b)/(z_P-b) preserves the current logit while using the prototype Gram shape, and beta=(z_P-b)/(z-b) targets the prototype logit while retaining the current Gram shape. Positive finite ratios, nonzero denominators, PSD roots, nondegenerate normalized Grams, float32 head rechecks, EQUAL sign preservation and original-H fallback are necessary registered guards. Selecting P by sign(z) does not guarantee a feasible positive ratio because b need not be zero.

R uses all qualified predeclared failure seeds as its repair denominator and separately requires zero registered harms among predeclared successes plus GAUGE local and long equivalence. M uses only EQUAL-feasible failure seeds as its conditional denominator and separately reports repair over the full original failure denominator. With only two eligible failures, the 0.8 rule requires both repairs; Wilson intervals and the actual denominators are needed. EQUAL harm among predeclared successes is reported but is not currently an M support gate, so any M support must remain explicitly conditional on the eligible failure stratum.

The supervised two-prototype codebook supplies labels and a finite-state prior. A successful EQUAL8 path would show repair under a constrained logit-preserving construction, not a unique shape cause or a general learned mechanism. SCALE8 and strong INV remain descriptive controls; neither R nor M is a Gate 1 verdict.

blocking.issue: M lacks the GAUGE8 equivalence qualification used for R, so its supported verdict can attribute a long-rollout coordinate-control effect to EQUAL8.
blocking.evidence: experiments/EXP-0025/v1.md:28 requires all qualified REL models to pass GAUGE8 local Gram/logit tolerances and final LONG mean equivalence to NONE for R. Line 29 defines M eligibility only by EQUAL8 event validity and Gram change. EXP-0024/v1.md:16 required both GAUGE checks for its frozen-case mechanism witness. Local Gram/logit equality after each GAUGE event alone does not prove long-rollout equivalence under float32 recurrence.
blocking.required_resolution: Before implementation or seed outcomes, require both GAUGE8 local tolerance on the registered cases/cells and final LONG mean accuracy equivalence to NONE (absolute difference <=0.005) for every seed counted as M eligible. Freeze how GAUGE failures affect M eligibility and the insufficient-eligible-seed branch; retain those seeds and report their EQUAL effects descriptively. If v1 is already frozen, make this a prospective versioned protocol amendment rather than silently changing v1.

implementation_checks: Verify learned readout coefficients and bias from the actual model; compute q and q_P from actual float32 logits, perform ratios in float64, and validate the resulting float32 state using the original head. For EQUAL compare post-logit to pre-logit; for SCALE compare post-logit to z_P. Compare normalized post-Gram to P for EQUAL and pre-Gram for SCALE, checking both normalizers and finite output before accepting an event.

Exercise zero or near-zero q/q_P, opposite-sign q/q_P despite matching sign(z), nonfinite or overflowing scale, degenerate Gram, PSD eigenvalue rejection/clamping, exact-zero sign, failed post-cast tolerance, and fallback to the untouched H. Save reasons and denominators so invalid events are never counted as successful interventions.

Score each time point using the pre-refresh logit; refresh only after t=8,16,... and never at t0. Verify NONE against original forward, target isolation from prototype selection, independent XOR targets, fixed seed/model matrix, and no checkpoint selection from monitors.

Audit R and M independently on frozen qualification strata, including final NONE failure nonrecurrence, EQUAL eligible/ineligible failures, harm among qualification successes, GAUGE local and long conditions, exact 2-seed and 0.8 boundaries, and the old reference exclusion. Preserve all 26 models and all five conditions regardless of eligibility.
interpretation_limits: This static review does not validate runtime, numerical feasibility frequency, observed repair or population generalization. With the stated amendment, M can support only a conditional rescue among independently qualified, EQUAL-feasible failures whose GAUGE control is equivalent; it cannot isolate Gram shape as the sole cause.
